reason: The text demonstrates that Yahweh's care and empathy extend to both the Hebrew leaders and the entire people. In verse 4, the community collectively prays 'Hear our God, for we are despised' (using inclusive 'we'), asking for restoration of honor for the whole community. In verse 14, Nehemiah (the leader) explicitly invokes God on behalf of the people and instructs them to fight 'for your brothers, your sons and your daughters, your wives and your houses'—demonstrating concern for families and households. Verse 6 states 'the heart of the people was on the work,' and verse 15 notes that 'God frustrated their counsel,' showing divine intervention on behalf of the entire community, not just leaders. The organization by families (verse 13-14) and the requirement for all to remain in Jerusalem for collective defense (verse 22) further indicate that Yahweh's protection encompasses the people as a unified body with their livelihoods and families at stake.
